title: a shim that bounces mail raises the trouble at its own address
intention: A shim that cannot fill mail (no such verb, a handler that raises, no receive) raises the trouble at its own address under the identity it already names in the bounce, so the receiver reports its own unfillable request and the sender's raise under that identity adds to the same trouble.
why: Measured 2026-11-10: cairn/tools/base/shim.py _bounce_to_sender posts the bounce with body.trouble named but raises nothing; only the sender's handle_bounce raises. Akien (open-b9037ca75019): the receiver issues the trouble and reports it to the caller, and the sender may add to it: 'writing is not safe, but appending is.'
traces_to: Outline 3.4.3.4 (the device that errs returns a pointer to the trouble; the receiver of that pointer can add details) and 3.4.3.5; Akien's answer open-b9037ca75019; Law 7.
how: In BaseShim._bounce_to_sender, before posting, call self.raise_trouble(identity, why=reason, detail={sender, original verb, envelope id}) inside a guard that prints to stderr and never stops the bounce. handle_bounce stays: its raise under the same identity is the sender's addition. Red-first proof over a spy bus.

clauses.claim: mail to an undeclared verb makes the receiving shim raise exactly one trouble whose identity is mail-<device>-has-no-verb-<verb>, its detail naming the sender, the verb and the envelope id, and the bounce it posts names the same identity in body.trouble
a handler that raises makes the receiving shim raise mail-<device>-verb-<verb>-raised, and the handler's own exception still propagates
mail with no verb to a device with no receive() makes the receiving shim raise mail-<device>-has-no-receive
when raise_trouble itself raises, the bounce is still posted, unchanged, and a line naming the identity goes to stderr
mail a declared verb answers raises no trouble, and every tooth in test_bounce_raises_the_mail_trouble.py passes unchanged

decisions.text: D1: cairn/tools/base/shim.py _bounce_to_sender: after its no-sender/no-bus early return, identity = trouble or f'mail-{self.device_id}-bounced'; try: self.raise_trouble(identity, why=reason, detail={'sender': sender, 'original_verb': envelope.get('verb', ''), 'envelope': envelope.get('id')}) except Exception as e: print a line naming identity and e to sys.stderr; then post the bounce exactly as today with body.trouble = identity. handle_bounce's comment says its raise is the sender's addition to the receiver's trouble (open-b9037ca75019).

D2: the proof cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_a_bouncing_shim_raises_its_own_trouble.py, red-first, one tooth per clause, PROVES {'eff2fb9810de': {'1': 'the_undeclared_verb_raises_at_the_receiver', '2': 'the_raising_handler_raises_at_the_receiver', '3': 'no_receive_raises_at_the_receiver', '4': 'a_failed_raise_still_bounces', '5': 'answered_mail_raises_nothing'}}}}; a spy bus and a fixture shim built as cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_bounce_raises_the_mail_trouble.py builds them, raise_trouble captured on the instance; tooth 5 runs that proof's main() in a subprocess; the house runner.

out: the cairn CLI's typo handling (outline 3.4.3.5: a log line, not a trouble)

measured.saw: _bounce_to_sender posts body.trouble and raises nothing; handle_bounce raises at the sender
